name: Workbench
description: The project schematic: one OpenPara project file (.opara) that holds parts, assemblies, analyses and the other tools as blocks on a canvas, with wires between their cells (the geometry of a part feeding the geometry of an analysis) and a status mark on every cell (up to date, incomplete, refresh needed, update needed, failed). Blocks lock to a grid and never overlap (there is always a gap of 40 between two blocks), a box selects several, a selection moves as one, and the wires follow and run round the blocks, never behind them. Opening an analysis block refreshes its geometry from the wired part or assembly when that changed (never the solve). The results of a Parametric Study can be wired into a Sheets block, and only the studies wired into it can be imported there. The PDF Editor and the Annotator are blocks too (no wires yet): the PDF Editor keeps the PDFs opened in it inside the project, the Annotator keeps a link to its project folder. Opens at the start in the Playground's Full dev mode. Under development: it comes with a LOAD EXAMPLE PROJECT button and a PROJECT REPORT. Results are not saved in the project: opening one never starts a computation, the cells say update needed until you press Update.
